title: Breeze Hill: a short-stay investment beside Gohtong Jaya.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #428 | BREEZE HILL, GENTING HIGHLANDS
excerpt: A 1,722-unit freehold mixed development on commercial title at Gohtong Jaya, designed for short-term stays, with three separate pools and two-bedroom units as the main layout.
takeaways: 1,722 freehold units over 90 shops, mostly 756 sq ft two-bedrooms at about RM900 psf.
Three pools, a 400 m jogging track and three drop-offs for checkout rush hours.
Weekend traffic and engine noise, plenty of new supply, and not a first-home product.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Breeze Hill has 1,722 units in two towers on 6.76 acres of freehold land, on commercial title above 90 shops priced from RM1.6 million to RM4.3 million; the ground-floor shops have sold out. It is designed for short-term stays: three drop-offs and separate retail and resident car parks for peak check-in and checkout hours, a speed ramp, and a facility deck with 50 m and 25 m pools, a kids' pool, a 400 m jogging track, an elderly gym and a flying fox.

Two-bedroom units dominate, because Sean says they earn the most when two families travel together. He viewed the 756 sq ft Type B, with a 5.13 m wide living, dining and kitchen space and views over the hills, at about RM900 psf; studios start from about RM400,000.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site is just past the Gohtong Jaya roundabout, beside its seafood restaurants and stalls, within the developer's 596-acre Tropicana Windcity. Genting Permai's shops are minutes away and Genting Premium Outlets about ten, with the cable car up to the casino resort. On weekends and holidays the area is crowded and parking is short.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Sean cites 28 million visitors a year against about 10,000 units of accommodation. Nightly rates he quotes run about RM250 for a studio and RM450 for a three-bedroom nearby, varying by season. Commercial title allows up to 85% financing, and the developer's hospitality arm can manage units. He suggests daily rates might yield 10% to 11%, but says to do your own sums.

standout.title: Designed around checkout time
standout.body: Research on similar buildings showed traffic peaking between noon and 3 pm as guests check in and out, so the project has three separate drop-offs, one for the shops and one for each tower, plus a dedicated exit and separate car parks for shoppers and residents.

pros: Genting Highlands: a destination nearly every Malaysian visits, about an hour from the Klang Valley. This site balances nature with convenience, with Gohtong Jaya's food, its own shops, Genting Permai and the outlets nearby, and good roads.
The developer's tourism approach, refined in Langkawi and Johor: a hospitality arm to manage units, and a clear reading of the gap between visitor numbers and rooms.

Design for the site: a mixed development, three drop-offs, speed ramps, separate access, and a facility deck with something for every age. The two-bedroom layout is open and the bathrooms are well specified.
cons: The micro site: the only entrance will jam at weekends and peak hours, and cars and sports-car exhausts are loud on the road. Sean would pick units facing the hills.
Density and competition: many new projects line the road up from KL. Anchor decisions on room and rental rates, as the developer does.
Not for first-time buyers: suited to investors who already own a home and a long-term rental, and who must choose between the developer's manager, an outside operator or running it themselves.

closing: Sean says it is beyond his expectations, and sees tourism-focused projects becoming a new strength for a developer that has survived COVID.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this February 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the show unit at the sales gallery as foundation works neared completion. Visitor numbers and nightly rates are as he quoted them.
